placement-retake-2026-07.title: Place yourself in any language — and again later
placement-retake-2026-07.body: Starting a new language now offers a short adaptive test so your queue fits you from day one instead of starting at A1. You can take it, or retake it, any time from Settings → Your level — the questions change each time, so a retake shows how far you’ve actually come.

language-facts-2026-07.title: Things to know about this language
language-facts-2026-07.body: A one-minute primer on the language you’re studying — its family, where it’s spoken, how its sentences are built, a short history, and what makes it distinctive. Right next to Letters & Sounds on your dashboard.

gym-adaptive-2026-07.title: The Gym adapts to you
gym-adaptive-2026-07.body: The Gym now learns from how you answer: forms you keep missing (and irregulars) come back more often, forms you’ve nailed fade. Opt into fresh sentences and it drafts brand-new drills in the background and weaves them into your set — no waiting.

learning-tips-2026-07.title: Learning tips
learning-tips-2026-07.body: Occasional, evidence-based nudges on how to study — read aloud, trust the spacing, mix it up — shown at most about once a day. Not for you? One switch in Settings turns them off.

review-audio-2026-07.title: Clearer, faster review audio
review-audio-2026-07.body: After you answer, the “word” and “full sentence” buttons are now labelled apart, and both clips are pre-loaded so they play the instant you tap — no more waiting on the sound.

korean-2026-07.title: Korean
korean-2026-07.body: Language #20 is live: 7,000 words, a 40-point grammar path from particles to honorifics, Hangul in Letters & Sounds, neural audio, the tutor, the Reader, and its own Gym. 한국어를 배워요!

gym-2026-07.title: The Gym
gym-2026-07.body: Pick the forms you want to train — past tense, accusative, whatever your language has — and drill them in a mixed bag. Stuck mid-question? Peek at the full conjugation chart. Russian first; more languages are on the way.

listening-gap-2026-07.title: Listening mode marks the gap
listening-gap-2026-07.body: The audio now pauses where the missing word belongs, and the sentence shape shows the blank — no more guessing where the word fell out.

daily-learn-goal-2026-07.title: A daily Learn goal
daily-learn-goal-2026-07.body: The Learn tile now counts toward a small daily target instead of showing the whole queue. Set it to 20, 50, or the full queue in Settings.

email-reminders-2026-07.title: Email review reminders
email-reminders-2026-07.body: Opt in to a daily digest of what is waiting for you — reviews due, streak status, one click back into the app.

welcome.title: Welcome — here’s the quick tour
welcome.body: A quick swipe through what’s here, then get learning. You can reopen this any time from the “?” on your dashboard.

language.title: Get to know your language
language.body: Letters & Sounds walks you through the script — every letter and how to say it (handy for Russian, Arabic, Greek, Hindi, Thai). Right beside it, Things to know about this language is a one-minute primer on its family, word order, history, and what makes it unique.

learnReview.title: Learn vs. Review
learnReview.body: Learn introduces new words and grammar. Review brings them back right before you’d forget — that spacing is what moves them into long-term memory. Learn a little, then let Review do the heavy lifting.

gym.title: The Gym
gym.body: Drill the forms your language bends — a tense, a case — in a mixed set. It adapts: the forms you miss come back more, the ones you’ve mastered fade. Turn on fresh sentences and it drafts brand-new drills in the background and weaves them in as you go.

tutor.title: Tutor — Practice vs. Reference
tutor.body: Practice drills you on the language and saves what you covered to your profile, so lessons build on each other. Reference is for a quick question — a straight answer, no drills, and nothing saved. Use Practice to study, Reference to just ask.

read.title: Read
read.body: Read short passages graded to your level and tap any word for its meaning — the fastest way to turn vocabulary into real reading.

ownText.title: Bring your own text
ownText.body: Paste something you actually want to read into the Reader — a song, an article, a message — and study the words that matter to you.

install.appBody: Use PolyglotSRS as an app — reviews one tap from your home screen.
install.iosBody: Add to your home screen: tap Share ⎋ then “Add to Home Screen”.

errorScreen.title: Something went wrong
errorScreen.body: Sorry — that page hit an error. Reloading usually fixes it, and your progress is saved on the server.

tips.footer: Learning tip · turn these off in Settings

read-aloud.title: Say it out loud
read-aloud.body: If you can, whisper or speak each sentence as you answer. Producing a word aloud makes it far stickier than reading it silently — it’s one of the simplest wins in learning.

retrieval.title: The struggle to recall is the point
retrieval.body: Pulling an answer from memory — even when you get it wrong — strengthens it more than re-reading ever could. That effort right before the reveal is where the learning happens.

shadow.title: Shadow the audio
shadow.body: Play a sentence and repeat it straight back, copying the rhythm and melody. It trains your ear and your mouth at the same time.

generation.title: Type it, don’t just recognise it
generation.body: Producing the answer yourself beats picking it from a list — that’s why the drills ask you to write it. The little bit of extra effort pays off in recall.

mistakes.title: Wrong answers are data, not failure
mistakes.body: Every miss tells the app exactly what to bring back sooner. Getting things wrong and correcting them is how the schedule tunes itself to you.

spacing.title: Short and often beats marathons
spacing.body: Ten focused minutes a day teaches you more than a two-hour weekend cram. Spacing your practice out is one of the most reliable findings in all of learning science.

trust-schedule.title: Trust the schedule
trust-schedule.body: Reviews come back just as you’re about to forget them. Returning right at that edge is what moves a word into long-term memory — so a quiet day of few reviews is the system working.

consistency.title: A streak beats a burst
consistency.body: Showing up daily, even briefly, keeps everything warm. Missed a day? Just pick back up — one lapse doesn’t undo your progress.

sleep.title: Sleep on it
sleep.body: Memory consolidates while you sleep. A short session in the evening, reviewed again the next morning, sticks better than the same minutes crammed back to back.

interleave.title: Mix it up
interleave.body: Jumping between tenses and topics — the way the Gym does — feels harder than drilling one thing, but it builds more flexible, longer-lasting knowledge.

elaborate.title: Make it mean something
elaborate.body: Tie a new word to an image, a little story, or a word you already know. The more hooks you give a word, the easier it is to find later.

in-context.title: Learn words inside sentences
in-context.body: A word met in a real sentence brings its grammar and its usual company along with it — far more useful than a bare translation on its own.
